sources: dossier=Net position bullet 6 (2026-06-22, 10cf843b, transcript) + Corrections-and-restorations entry, explicitly pre-adjudicated fix-doc for this finding (2026-07-13, 3f71f90a, transcript); doc=error-policy.md:14 claimed error routing is the 'single' decision surface matched against the per-class action map for 'every error variant', and :35 said infra errors apply the supervisor cap only 'when no operator policy is declared for the class'; code=runner_terminal.go:48/72 routes terminalKindInfra to applyTerminalInfraError (runner_error_policy.go:180-218), which never looks up acq.NodeDef.ErrorTypes -- it always uses resolveRetryConfig(acq.NodeDef) as a plain numeric MaxRetries, falling back to defaultInfraRetryCap(10) only when unset; test=none consulted, dossier corroboration sufficed.
note: Dossier explicitly rules infra-class errors bypass the per-class action map entirely (terminal-resolution owns them), with a supervisor default cap of 10 overridden by an operator's node-level MaxRetries when set -- and states this exact finding (54) was already adjudicated fix-doc on 2026-07-13. Rewrote the 'What it is' single-decision-surface claim and the MaxRetries/infra invariant to match.

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 8 (2026-06-11, last-mile-stability, artifact): 'a key attributable to no declared vocabulary registers with an advisory warning, never a hard rejection... declaring nothing remains legal'; doc=error-policy.md:16 described only the advisory-warning-vs-hard-rejection axis; code=template_validator.go:344-368, vocabularyKnown stays false and the loop continues with no Warnings append when neither the executor nor any producer returns a declared vocabulary (ok=true), producing silence rather than a warning.
note: The dossier's 'declaring nothing remains legal' framing is coherent with a third, silent behavior when no peer declares any vocabulary at all (nothing to range-check against), but the dossier entry itself is artifact-tier and doesn't spell out this specific edge case, so provenance is artifact-only rather than corroborated. Not design-incoherent, so ruled defect rather than design-call; added a clarifying sentence distinguishing the zero-vocabulary silent case from the advisory-warning case.

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 6 uses 'Infrastructure-class errors' as a term of art distinct from operator-declared error policy, owned by terminal-resolution (2026-06-22, 10cf843b, transcript); doc's own Boundaries section already cites concept:terminal-resolution for 'stitching from terminal event to producer verb'; doc=error-policy.md:35 used 'Infra-class errors' and 'operator-side errors' without defining either.
note: The split is real and dossier/boundary-corroborated (infra-class = runtime-synthesized dispatch faults owned by terminal-resolution; operator-side = per-class-action-map-routed errors), just previously undefined in the concept body. Folded a definition into the same invariant edited for row 54 rather than leaving the terms free-floating.

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 4 and Required-behaviors bullet 2: 'Claim-acquisition errors retry in-place through the exact same machinery as executor errors -- one unified path' (2026-06-22, 10cf843b, transcript); doc=error-policy.md:39 worded the retry invariant exclusively for the executor surface ('re-invokes the executor... node-run stays in state running'); code=runner_acquire.go:212-257 acquireOneCandidateWithRetry loops on tryAcquireWithTx pre-dispatch, with the row in state stale, matching decision:in-place-retry's documented acquire surface.
note: Dossier (transcript-tier) confirms acquisition-failure retries share the same in-place-retry mechanism as executor retries but the row sits in a different node-run state (stale, not running) during the loop. Generalized the invariant to name both surfaces and their respective states instead of asserting 'running' universally.

sources: dossier=Required-behaviors bullet 2: a held-participating run that exhausts retries 'routes through give_up, whose lock release with success=false poisons the claim and auto-terminal abandons all holders' (2026-06-22, 10cf843b, transcript); independent design artifact concept:auto-terminal (Boundaries + Poison-rule invariant) confirms held claims defer the Commit/Abandon verb to the auto-terminal resolution engine rather than firing it immediately per-holder; doc=error-policy.md:36 said release-and-requeue releases held claim handles 'firing each producer's abandon verb'; code=runner_terminal_release.go releaseClaim: the isAliasHeld branch (shared by both give_up's and release-and-requeue's success=false release path) calls markClaimHolderForRun + FailAllActiveByClaimHandle + CheckAndFireResolution instead of an immediate OutcomeAbandon; only the non-held branch (:166-168) takes the direct abandon path.
note: Two independent design artifacts (the transcript-tier dossier describing give_up's held-claim mechanism, and concept:auto-terminal's own held-claim deferral invariants) corroborate that held claims never get an immediate abandon-verb fire; release_and_requeue shares the identical release codepath. Reworded the invariant to distinguish the immediate (non-held) and deferred-to-auto-terminal (held-subgraph) cases, and to stop overloading 'held' by naming the auto-terminal concept directly.
